flagged.title: Energy Stores, Transfers and Power
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly instructs students that g on Earth is always 10 N/kg, which will cause them to lose marks on AQA exams where g is specified as 9.8 N/kg.

mark_affecting.quote: remember that on Earth, g is always 10 N/kg

flagged.title: Circuits: Current, Resistance and Potential Difference
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims that V = I x R only applies to ohmic conductors at constant temperature, which can lead students to wrongly believe V = IR cannot be used to calculate resistance for non-ohmic components like filament lamps.

mark_affecting.quote: This perfect mathematical relationship only applies to ohmic conductors provided the temperature remains perfectly constant.

flagged.title: Domestic Electricity, Power and the National Grid
flagged.reason: The video directly teaches the named misconception that a 50 Hz alternating current changes direction 50 times per second instead of 100 times per second, which would lose a student marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: means the current literally changes direction 50 times every single second
